![Qwen Code in the terminal, desktop app, browser, editor, and chat, with VS Code, Zed, JetBrains, Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, and Feishu integrations](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i1/O1CN01DXWdF8BDUdD3XPhl_!!6000000001721-2-tps-1743-902.png) | **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview** | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together the agent harness capabilities of [Qoder](https://qoder.com/) and Qwen Code in an open-source release.

[Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview) · [Documentation](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/) · [中文文档](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/zh/users/overview/). | ## Why Qwen Code? - **Agentic out of the box** — Auto-Memory, Skills, SubAgents, and MCP work from the first session. Agent Teams, Agent Arena, and Dynamic Workflows are built in too — experimental or opt-in, as noted in [Capabilities](#capabilities). - **Open-source, inside and out** — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. - **Multi-protocol** — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. - **Beyond the terminal** — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / WeCom / Feishu and more). > [!TIP] > Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI. ## Installation Looking for **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview**? [Get started here](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview). The instructions below are for the main version. **Linux / macOS:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash ``` **Windows:** ```powershell irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex ``` > Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.
NPM / Homebrew **NPM** (requires [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/)): ```bash npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest ``` **Homebrew** (macOS / Linux): ```bash brew install qwen-code ```
## Quick Start Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code: ```bash cd /path/to/your-project qwen ``` Inside the session, run `/auth` and choose [**Qwen Account with Subscription**](https://chat.qwen.ai/?memberPlan=qwen_code&entry=qwen_code&paywallScene=cli) to sign in with your **Plus or Pro subscription**, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try: ```text Explain this repository and show me where to start. ``` See the [Authentication Guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/) and [Settings Reference](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/settings/) for detailed setup.
See the terminal interface ![Qwen Code terminal interface](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01K0nwj41RM1Il8kB0t_!!6000000002096-2-tps-1544-1060.png)
## How to Use Qwen Code Choose the interface that fits your workflow: | Interface | Get started | | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Terminal** | Run `qwen` in your project — see [Quick Start](#quick-start). | | **Desktop** | [Download Qwen Code Desktop](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/desktop-latest) for macOS, Windows, and Linux. | | **Web** | Run `qwen serve --open` to open the [Web UI](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/) in your browser. _(experimental)_ | | **Editor** | Set up [VS Code](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-vscode/), [Zed](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-zed/), or [JetBrains](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-jetbrains/). | | **Chat** | Connect [Telegram](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/telegram/), [DingTalk](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/dingtalk/), [WeChat](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/weixin/), [WeCom](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/wecom/), [Feishu](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/feishu/), [QQ Bot](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/qqbot/), [Email](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/email/), or [GitHub](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/github/), then run `qwen channel start`. See the [Channels overview](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/overview/) for webhook senders and plugin adapters. | For automation and custom integrations: - **Headless** — Run `qwen -p "..."` in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs. - **SDKs** — Build with [TypeScript](./packages/sdk-typescript/README.md), [Python](./packages/sdk-python/README.md), or [Java](./packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md). - **Daemon** — Run `qwen serve` to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). _(experimental)_ [Daemon guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/). - **Computer Use** — Set up [native MCP tools](./packages/cua-driver/README.md#agent-integration) or [Node REPL + SDK](./packages/node-repl/README.md#usage) in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python) ```python import asyncio from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query async def main() -> None: result = query( "Summarize the repository layout.", { "cwd": "/path/to/project", "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen", }, ) async for message in result: if is_sdk_result_message(message): print(message["result"]) asyncio.run(main()) ```
## Daemon Mode Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions. Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell: ```bash qwen serve --open ``` The default address is `http://127.0.0.1:4170`. To run and manage it in the background instead: ```bash qwen daemon start qwen daemon status qwen daemon logs -f qwen daemon stop ``` By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` and use `--require-auth`. See the [Daemon guide](./docs/users/qwen-serve.md) for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API. ## Capabilities Qwen Code ships with a complete agent harness — multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, and deep extensibility, all built in. ### Agentic core - **[SubAgents](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/sub-agents/)** — delegate focused subtasks to specialized agents with their own context and toolsets, in the foreground or background. - **[Agent Teams](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/multi-agent-coordination/)** _(experimental)_ — a leader coordinates teammates that share a task list and exchange messages, with read-only investigators and an optional single worktree writer. - **[Agent Arena](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/arena/)** _(experimental)_ — run the same task on multiple models in isolated Git worktrees, compare solutions side by side, and merge the winner. - **[Dynamic Workflows](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/workflow-mode/)** _(opt-in)_ — the model writes JavaScript workflows that orchestrate agents: parallel fan-out, verification passes, and resumable runs. - **[Goals](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/goals/)** — `/goal` keeps the session working across turns until an independent verifier accepts the outcome, within a token budget. - **[Scheduled tasks](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/scheduled-tasks/)** — `/loop` and cron tools re-run prompts on an interval or at a set time. ### Memory, skills, and sessions - **[Auto-Memory](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/memory/)** — the agent writes its own notes and recalls them across sessions; your `QWEN.md` and `AGENTS.md` briefings load automatically. - **[Skills & Auto-Skills](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/skills/)** — built-in skills (`/review`, `/batch`, `/bugfix`…) work out of the box; `/learn` distills docs or code into new skills, the agent can generate skills on its own _(opt-in)_, and `/curator` maintains the library. - **[Session management](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/session-overview/)** — resume past conversations with [`/resume`](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/commands/), and browse, rename, or archive sessions. ### Multimodal - **[Voice input](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/voice-input/)** — dictate prompts in the terminal or Web Shell with a configurable ASR model; the Web Shell inserts the transcript for review before sending. - **[Qwen Live](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/qwen-live/)** _(experimental)_ — realtime speech-to-speech conversations in the Web Shell that answer directly or hand tasks to the agent, with optional screen sharing. - **[Image generation](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/image-generation/)** — the built-in `image_gen` tool turns prompts into PNG artifacts using your configured image model. ### Extensibility and control - **[Hooks](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/hooks/)** — run your own scripts at lifecycle events: before and after tool calls, session start and end, and more. - **[MCP](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/mcp/)** — connect any Model Context Protocol server to add tools, resources, and prompts. - **[LSP integration](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/lsp/)** _(experimental, opt-in)_ — native language-server support: go-to-definition, references, diagnostics, and code actions. - **[Computer Use & Browser Use](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/computer-use/)** — automate desktop applications and the browser through native MCP tools. - **[Plan Mode & approval modes](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/approval-mode/)** — plan read-only before touching files, then choose per-call confirmation, auto-edit, classifier-driven [Auto Mode](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/auto-mode/), or YOLO. - **[Sandbox](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/sandbox/) & [Git worktrees](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/worktree/)** — confine tool execution with built-in sandboxing and isolate wide-ran
